categories.main_business_segments: CenterPoint Energy operates two primary business segments: Electric and Natural Gas. The Electric segment includes electric transmission and distribution services in Texas (Houston Electric) and Indiana (SIGECO/Indiana Electric), as well as electric generation assets in Indiana. The Natural Gas segment provides regulated intrastate natural gas sales, transportation, and distribution services across Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Ohio, and Texas. The company also has a smaller Corporate and Other segment, which includes energy performance contracting and sustainable infrastructure services through Energy Systems Group.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operations rely on regulated electric transmission and distribution infrastructure, including high-voltage lines, substations, and advanced metering systems, as well as natural gas distribution pipelines and storage facilities. Indiana Electric owns and operates coal, gas, and renewable (solar, landfill gas) generation assets, and is transitioning toward more renewables and natural gas. The company employs advanced metering infrastructure (AMI/AMS), grid modernization, and pipeline integrity management programs to ensure reliability and safety.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CenterPoint Energy primarily serves residential, commercial, industrial, and transportation customers. In Texas, its electric customers are retail electric providers (REPs) who supply end-users in the Houston/Galveston area, while in Indiana, it serves direct retail customers. Its natural gas business serves over 4 million customers, including major metropolitan areas such as Houston, Minneapolis, Shreveport, Biloxi, Evansville, and Dayton. Key end markets include residential heating, commercial and industrial energy needs, and utility-scale power generation.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are concentrated in the U.S., with electric transmission and distribution in the Houston, Texas area and southwestern Indiana, and natural gas distribution across Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Ohio, and Texas. Its largest electric service territory is the Houston/Galveston metropolitan area, and its natural gas footprint covers major cities in the listed states. The company does not have significant international operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: CenterPoint Energy operates primarily as a downstream utility, delivering electricity and natural gas to end-users. In electric operations, it functions as a transmission and distribution utility (TDU) in Texas and as a vertically integrated utility (generation, transmission, distribution) in Indiana. In natural gas, it is a local distribution company (LDC), purchasing gas from upstream suppliers and delivering it to customers. The company does not own significant upstream production or midstream assets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, CenterPoint Energy is focused on regulated utility growth, grid modernization, system resiliency, and the transition to cleaner energy. The company has announced a 10-year capital plan exceeding $40 billion, with significant investments in renewables, grid upgrades, and infrastructure reliability. It has set net zero emissions goals for Scope 1 and certain Scope 2 emissions by 2035 and aims to reduce certain Scope 3 emissions by 20-30% by 2035. R&D and innovation efforts are directed toward renewable integration, advanced metering, and pipeline safety.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through regulated rates for electric transmission and distribution services and natural gas sales and transportation. Electric revenues are collected from REPs (in Texas) and direct customers (in Indiana) based on energy delivered and peak demand, while natural gas revenues are derived from volumetric sales and transportation charges to residential, commercial, and industrial customers. Rates are set and periodically adjusted by state and local regulators, with some pass-through of fuel and purchased gas costs.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In its core service territories, CenterPoint Energy faces limited direct competition due to exclusive or semi-exclusive utility franchises. In Texas and Indiana, it is the sole provider of electric T&D in its service areas, and in natural gas, it competes with alternative energy sources and, in some areas, other gas distributors and marketers. Major competitors in adjacent or overlapping markets include other regulated utilities and energy providers such as Atmos Energy, Xcel Energy, and regional electric cooperatives. The company is positioned as a leading regulated utility in its regions, with over 7 million metered customers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: CenterPoint Energy is a large-cap utility with total revenues of $9.3 billion in 2022 and net income available to common shareholders of $1.0 billion. The company serves over 7 million metered customers and has a market capitalization of approximately $18.5 billion as of mid-2022. Its growth profile is driven by regulated utility investments, customer growth (2% in electric, 1% in gas), and a multi-year capital plan focused on infrastructure and clean energy transition. The company has divested non-core businesses to focus on regulated operations, with over 95% of earnings now from regulated utilities.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CenterPoint Energy emphasizes safe, reliable, and affordable energy delivery, with a strong focus on system resiliency, customer service, and environmental stewardship. Its value proposition includes leading grid modernization, a commitment to net zero emissions, and significant investments in clean energy and infrastructure reliability. The company differentiates itself through its scale, regulatory expertise, and proactive approach to sustainability and innovation, aiming to deliver long-term value to customers, communities, and shareholders.
